questions.prompt: “Nothing in this statement should be construed as an admission of liability.” What is the intended effect?
options: It confirms liability while disputing the amount.
It admits that the statement is legally inaccurate.
It transfers liability to the reader.
It prevents the statement from being treated as conceding liability.
questions.explanation: “Should be construed as” concerns interpretation; the clause expressly blocks an inference of admitted liability.
questions.targetConstruct: Use reading to resolve ““Nothing in this statement should be construed as an admission of liability.” What is the intended effect?” in the context “Legal non-admission clause”.
questions.cefrRationale: C2 text task: the learner handles “Legal non-admission clause” and identifies “It prevents the statement from being treated as conceding liability.” using the stated reading cue.
questions.ambiguityNotes: Only “It prevents the statement from being treated as conceding liability.” satisfies the stated context and target; the distractors conflict with the prompt or this rule: “Should be construed as” concerns interpretation; the clause expressly blocks an inference of admitted liability.
